title: Press Release - AMLA consults on AML/CFT supervisory colleges in the EU

paras.text: The Authority for Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (AMLA) Messeturm Frankfurt, Friedrich-Ebert-Anlage 49, 60308 Frankfurt am Main, GERMANY email: media@amla.europa.eu | amla.europa.eu PRESS RELEASE Frankfurt am Main, 23 November 2026 AMLA consults on AML/CFT supervisory colleges in the EU AMLA has launched two public consultations on draft Regulatory Technical Standards (RTSs) for the functioning of AML/CFT supervisory colleges in the financial and non-financial sectors. The standards provide a framework for cooperation, coordination and information exchange between supervisors responsible for the oversight of entities or groups operating in more than one Member State.

Building on experience in the financial sector For the financial sector, the draft standards build on the core elements of the AML/CFT Colleges Guidelines, which the European Supervisory Authorities issued in 2019. Previous reports by the European Banking Authority, AMLA's participation in college meetings and feedback from national authorities all demonstrate that AML/CFT supervisory colleges play a key role in cross -border supervision. The draft standards aim to strengthen that role through risk-based supervisory cooperation, greater legal clarity, improved cooperation mechanisms, and reduced administrative burdens for supervisors.

A tailored approach for the non-financial sector Unlike the financial sector, the non-financial sector does not yet have an established framework for AML/CFT supervisory college s. Instead, AML/CFT supervisory colleges in the nonfinancial sector may be established on a voluntary basis. The draft standards are designed to support authorities that choose to do so. They build on the framework developed for the financial sector, with targeted and proportionate adaptations for the non-financial sector. Shaping the final standards Both consultations are open until 23 December 2026. The draft standards concern cooperation between supervisors and have no direct impact on businesses and professionals covered by antimoney laundering rules. AMLA particularly welcomes input from financial and nonfinancial supervisors, including self-regulatory bodies. Contributions can be submitted via the EU Survey for the financial and non-financial sectors. Public hearings will take place on 14 December 2026: the financial sector session from 10:00 to 12:00 CET and the non-financial sector session from 14:00 to 16:00 CET.
For media queries, please contact media@amla.europa.eu
